title: How to Build a Retirement Plan If You Anticipate High Longevity (100+)
description: Asset allocation for a 40-year distribution phase.
content:
Living to 100 is a blessing, but it breaks most standard financial plans. A 'Safe Withdrawal Rate' of 4% is designed for 30 years. If you live 40 or 45 years in retirement, that rate has a high failure probability. You face the 'Triple Threat': Inflation eroding purchasing power, Sequence of Returns risk over a longer window, and the massive cost of late-life care. Centenarian planning requires a portfolio that acts like an endowment: designed to grow forever, not spend down to zero.

Key Takeaways

  • Lower Withdrawal Rate: For a 40+ year horizon, safe withdrawal rates drop to 3.0% - 3.3%. You need a larger nest egg ($1.5M to generate $50k, not $1.25M).
  • High Equity Exposure: You cannot hold 60% bonds. Inflation over 40 years will cut your dollar's value by 70%. You need 60-70% stocks even at age 80 to generate the growth required to stay ahead of prices.
  • Longevity Insurance (QLAC): Buy a Qualified Longevity Annuity Contract. You pay at 65, it pays starting at 85. This guarantees you have income in the 'Danger Zone' years.
  • Delay Social Security: Claiming at 70 is mandatory. It gives you the highest possible inflation-adjusted floor. If you live to 100, this decision is worth hundreds of thousands of dollars.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The fastest-growing demographic in the US is Centenarians. Advances in medicine mean 'Old' is getting older. Planning for 95 is the new conservative standard.

The Endowment Model

Your money must outlive you.

The Inflation Problem

At 3% inflation, a $50,000 lifestyle today costs $162,000 in 40 years.
Bonds earning 4% barely keep up. Stocks earning 8% are the only way to generate that future cash flow.

The Rising Equity Glidepath

Standard advice: Sell stocks, buy bonds as you age.
Longevity Advice: Buy stocks as you age.
Start retirement at 60/40. As your time horizon extends, move to 70/30 or 80/20. You are investing for your 100-year-old self.

The 'Care' Fund

Living to 100 guarantees frailty. You need a dedicated bucket ($300k+) for home health aides. If you don't use it, your heirs get it.

Tactical Steps

  1. Buy a QLAC: Take $200k of your IRA. Buy an annuity that starts at 85. This takes 'running out of money' off the table for the super-old years.
  2. Health Investment: Spend money on fitness/nutrition now. Compressing morbidity (being sick for 2 years instead of 10) saves massive amounts of money.
  3. Variable Spending: Be flexible. In a bad market decade, spend 2.5%. In a good decade, spend 4%. Rigidity kills longevity portfolios.
  4. Reverse Mortgage Standby: Keep your home equity as the ultimate backup. A HECM line of credit grows over time and can fund care at age 98.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I die at 80?

Then you leave a huge inheritance. That is a 'good' failure mode. Running out of money at 95 is a 'bad' failure mode. Plan for the worst (living long).

Is 3% withdrawal too low?

It feels low, but it ensures survival. To spend more, you might need a side hustle or rental income. Don't rely on principal drain.

Should I buy LTC insurance?

Yes. Extreme longevity correlates with cognitive decline. Insurance protects your spouse from your care costs.
